ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا اخْتَلَفْتُمْ فِيهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَحُكْمُهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبِّي عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ (١٠)).
His saying (ذَلِكُمُ): it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with «اللَّهُ» an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) or a badal (substitute), and «رَبِّي» the khabar (predicate). Or اللَّهُ may be the khabar, with رَبِّي a second khabar or a badal; or [رَبِّي] may be an adjective of [the name] Allah the Exalted, and «عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ» the khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ جَعَلَ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَنْفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا وَمِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ أَزْوَاجًا يَذْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْبَصِيرُ (١١)).
His saying (فَاطِرُ السَّمَاوَاتِ): i.e. "He is the Originator"; it may also be a further khabar (predicate).
It is also read in the genitive (فَاطِرِ), as a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in «عَلَيْهِ». The hāʾ in «فِيهِ» is the pronoun of the making (al-jaʿl), which the verb has indicated; it may also be the pronoun of the created thing indicated by يَذْرَؤُكُمْ.
The kāf in «كَمِثْلِهِ» is redundant (zāʾida), i.e. "nothing is like Him" (لَيْسَ مِثْلَهُ شَيْءٌ); so مِثْلَهُ is the khabar of لَيْسَ. If it were not redundant, it would lead to an impossibility, since the meaning would then be that He has a like, and that His like has no like; and in that there is a contradiction, because if He has a like, then His like has a like, namely Him — besides the fact that affirming a like for Allah, glory be to Him, is impossible.
It is also said: «مِثْلِ» is redundant, and the implied wording is "nothing is as He is" (لَيْسَ كَهُوَ شَيْءٌ), as in His saying (فَإِنْ آمَنُوا بِمِثْلِ مَا آمَنْتُمْ بِهِ); this has been mentioned. This is a far-fetched view.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (شَرَعَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الدِّينِ مَا وَصَّى بِهِ نُوحًا وَالَّذِي أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ وَمَا وَصَّيْنَا بِهِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَمُوسَى وَعِيسَى أَنْ أَقِيمُوا الدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا فِيهِ كَبُرَ عَلَى الْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ اللَّهُ يَجْتَبِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي إِلَيْهِ مَنْ يُنِيبُ (١٣)).
His saying (أَنْ أَقِيمُوا): it may be a badal (substitute) of the hāʾ in «بِهِ», or of «مَا», or of «مِنَ الدِّينِ» — each is suitable.
It may also be that «أَنْ» has the sense of أَيْ ("that is"), so that it has no grammatical position.

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ وَالْمِيزَانَ وَمَا يُدْرِيكَ لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ (١٧)).
His saying (لَعَلَّ السَّاعَةَ قَرِيبٌ): it may have been put in the masculine according to the meaning of "the time", or according to the meaning of "the resurrection", or as a relational form (al-nasab), i.e. "possessed of nearness".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (تَرَى الظَّالِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا كَسَبُوا وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ بِهِمْ وَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فِي رَوْضَاتِ الْجَنَّاتِ لَهُمْ مَا يَشَاءُونَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْفَضْلُ الْكَبِيرُ (٢٢)).
(وَهُوَ وَاقِعٌ): i.e. the requital of what they earned.
It is also said: it is the pronoun of the fearing (al-ishfāq).

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ الَّذِي يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ عِبَادَهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ قُلْ لَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ فِي الْقُرْبَى وَمَنْ يَقْتَرِفْ حَسَنَةً نَزِدْ لَهُ فِيهَا حُسْنًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ شَكُورٌ (٢٣)).
His saying (يُبَشِّرُ اللَّهُ): the pronoun referring back to الَّذِي is omitted, i.e. "gives glad tidings of it".
(إِلَّا الْمَوَدَّةَ): a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), or the reverse [Translator's note: so in the text]. It is also said: it is a connected exception, i.e. "I do not ask you for anything except love for kinship, for that I do ask of you".

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَمْ يَقُولُونَ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا فَإِنْ يَشَأِ اللَّهُ يَخْتِمْ عَلَى قَلْبِكَ وَيَمْحُ اللَّهُ الْبَاطِلَ وَيُحِقُّ الْحَقَّ بِكَلِمَاتِهِ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (٢٤)).
His saying (يَخْتِمْ): it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (وَيَمْحُ): nominative, resumptive, and not part of the apodosis, because He erases falsehood without condition. The wāw was dropped from the pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, and from the Muṣḥaf by following the pronunciation.

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيَسْتَجِيبُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتُ وَيَزِيدُهُمْ مِنْ فَضْلِهِ وَالْكَافِرُونَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ (٢٦)).
His saying (وَيَسْتَجِيبُ): it means "He answers".
And (الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا) is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
It is also said: "He answers the prayer of those who believe".
It is also said: «الَّذِينَ» is in the position of the nominative, i.e. they submit to Him.

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ خَلْقُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَثَّ فِيهِمَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ وَهُوَ عَلَى جَمْعِهِمْ إِذَا يَشَاءُ قَدِيرٌ (٢٩)).
His saying (إِذَا يَشَاءُ): what governs «إِذَا» is «جَمْعِهِمْ», not «قَدِيرٌ», because that would lead to the meaning becoming "and He is able to gather them when He wills", so that the power would be made dependent on the will; and that is impossible.
«عَلَى» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to قَدِيرٌ.

ukberi-tibyan:3-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ اللَّهُ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ (٣) لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ (٤)).
His saying (كَذَلِكَ يُوحِي): it is read with a yāʾ with ḍamma, in the active voice (ʿalā mā summiya fāʿiluhu, "with its agent named"); the fāʿil (agent) is (اللَّهُ) and what follows it is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and the kāf is in the position of the accusative by يُوحِي. It is also read in the passive (يُوحَى), and there are two views on that. The first: that «كَذَلِكَ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «يُوحَى» the khabar (predicate), and «اللَّهُ» is the agent of an omitted verb, as though it were asked "Who reveals?" and He said: "Allah"; and what follows it is a naʿt of it.
It is also possible that «الْعَزِيزُ» is a mubtadaʾ, with «الْحَكِيمُ» a naʿt of it or a khabar, and «لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ» a khabar, or a second khabar. The second view: that «كَذَلِكَ» is a naʿt of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), and «إِلَيْكَ» is what stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent); i.e. "a revelation like that".

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ مِنْ مُصِيبَةٍ فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَيَعْفُو عَنْ كَثِيرٍ (٣٠)).
His saying (وَمَا أَصَابَكُمْ): «مَا» is conditional, in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(فَبِمَا كَسَبَتْ) is its apodosis (jawāb), and what is meant by the two verbs is the future. Whoever among the Readers dropped the fāʾ (بِمَا كَسَبَتْ) construed it on the pattern of His saying (وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ), and of what occurs in the poet's saying:
مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الْحَسَنَاتِ اللَّهُ يَشْكُرُهَا
("Whoever does good deeds, Allah will thank them")
On this view, «مَا» may also be taken in the sense of الَّذِي (that which), but there is weakness in that.

ukberi-tibyan:32-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ الْجَوَارِ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ (٣٢) إِنْ يَشَأْ يُسْكِنِ الرِّيحَ فَيَظْلَلْنَ رَوَاكِدَ عَلَى ظَهْرِهِ إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِكُلِّ صَبَّارٍ شَكُورٍ (٣٣) أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ بِمَا كَسَبُوا وَيَعْفُ عَنْ كَثِيرٍ (٣٤) وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ يُجَادِلُونَ فِي آيَاتِنَا مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ (٣٥)).
His saying (الْجِوَارِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), or a fāʿil (agent) made nominative by the preposition phrase; and «فِي الْبَحْرِ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it, governed by [the notion of] settledness (al-istiqrār). «فِي» may also be attached (mutaʿalliq) to الْجَوَارِي.
And (كَالْأَعْلَامِ) is, on the first view, a second ḥāl, and on the second it is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «الْجَوَارِ». And (يُسْكِنِ) is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (فَيَظْلَلْنَ) is conjoined to the apodosis, and likewise «أَوْ يُوبِقْهُنَّ» and «يَعْفُ».
As for His saying (وَيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ): it is read in the accusative on the implied wording "and that He may know" (وَأَنْ يَعْلَمَ), because He turned it away from the apodosis and conjoined it according to the meaning.
It is also read with kasra (وَيَعْلَمِ), on the view that it is jussive (majzūm), vowelled because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. It is also read in the nominative (وَيَعْلَمُ), as resumptive. His saying (مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ مَحِيصٍ): the negated clause stands in place of the two objects of عَلِمْتُ.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَمَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ خَيْرٌ وَأَبْقَى لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying (فَمَتَاعُ الْحَيَاةِ): i.e. "then it is enjoyment".

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ كَبَائِرَ الْإِثْمِ وَالْفَوَاحِشَ وَإِذَا مَا غَضِبُوا هُمْ يَغْفِرُونَ (٣٧)).
His saying (وَالَّذِينَ يَجْتَنِبُونَ): conjoined to His saying (لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَلَى رَبِّهِمْ يَتَوَكَّلُونَ).
It may also be in the position of the accusative by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or of the nominative on the implied wording «هُمْ» ("they are").
And (كَبَائِرَ) is in the plural, its singular being كَبِيرَةٌ; whoever read it in the singular (كَبِيرَ) took it as the genus.
And (هُمْ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «يَغْفِرُونَ» is the khabar (predicate), and the clause is the answer to إِذَا.
It is also said: «هُمْ» is nominative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "they forgave" (غَفَرُوا); the verb was omitted because يَغْفِرُونَ indicates it.

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَمَنْ صَبَرَ وَغَفَرَ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِنْ عَزْمِ الْأُمُورِ (٤٣)).
His saying (وَلَمَنْ صَبَرَ): «مَنْ» is conditional, and «صَبَرَ» is in the position of the jussive by it; the apodosis is (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ), the fāʾ having been omitted.
It is also said: «مَنْ» has the sense of الَّذِي (the one who), and the referring pronoun is omitted, i.e. "that, on his part, is…" (إِنَّ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُ).

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لَهُمْ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ سَبِيلٍ (٤٦)).
His saying (يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ): it may be in the position of the genitive, following the wording of the noun it qualifies, or in the nominative following its position.

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَإِنْ أَعْرَضُوا فَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظًا إِنْ عَلَيْكَ إِلَّا الْبَلَاغُ وَإِنَّا إِذَا أَذَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنَّا رَحْمَةً فَرِحَ بِهَا وَإِنْ تُصِبْهُمْ سَيِّئَةٌ بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ فَإِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ (٤٨)).
His saying (فَإِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ كَفُورٌ): i.e. "man among them" (إِنَّ الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْهُمْ) [Translator's note: i.e. the overt noun stands in place of the pronoun referring to them, with the referring element implied].

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَوْ يُزَوِّجُهُمْ ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَاثًا وَيَجْعَلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ عَقِيمًا إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ قَدِيرٌ (٥٠)).
His saying (ذُكْرَانًا وَإِنَاثًا): they are a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning is: He pairs the two kinds together.

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَّا وَحْيًا أَوْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ رَسُولًا فَيُوحِيَ بِإِذْنِهِ مَا يَشَاءُ إِنَّهُ عَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ (٥١)).
His saying (أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ اللَّهُ): «أَنْ» with the verb is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it is the khabar (predicate); or it is a fāʿil (agent) of the preposition phrase, since that leans on the particle of negation. And (إِلَّا وَحْيًا) is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because revelation (waḥy) is not speaking (taklīm).
(أَوْ مِنْ وَرَاءِ حِجَابٍ): the preposition is attached (mutaʿalliq) to something omitted, its implied form being "or that He speak to him"; and this omitted element is conjoined to «وَحْيًا», the implied wording being "except that it be revealed to him, or that He speak to him". «مِنْ» cannot be attached to the يُكَلِّمَهُ present in the wording, because what precedes a disconnected exception does not govern what comes after «إِلَّا».
As for (أَوْ يُرْسِلَ): whoever read it in the accusative [takes it as] conjoined to the position of «وَحْيًا», i.e. He sends an angel to him.
It is also said: it is in the position of the genitive, i.e. "by His sending" (بِأَنْ يُرْسِلَ). It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It cannot be conjoined to «أَنْ يُكَلِّمَهُ», because its meaning would then become "it is not for a human being that Allah should speak to him, nor that He should send a messenger to him", and this is unsound; and also because conjoining it to the أَنْ يُكَلِّمَ that is present would bring it into the ṣila (relative clause) of أَنْ, and «إِلَّا وَحْيًا» would separate one part of the ṣila from another, since it is disconnected.
Whoever read يُرْسِلُ in the nominative made it resumptive.
It is also said: «مِنْ» is attached to يُكَلِّمَهُ, because it is an adverbial phrase, and latitude is allowed with adverbial phrases.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ رُوحًا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا مَا كُنْتَ تَدْرِي مَا الْكِتَابُ وَلَا الْإِيمَانُ وَلَكِنْ جَعَلْنَاهُ نُورًا نَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ نَشَاءُ مِنْ عِبَادِنَا وَإِنَّكَ لَتَهْدِي إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٥٢)).
His saying (مَا كُنْتَ تَدْرِي): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf in «إِلَيْكَ».

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ أَلَا إِلَى اللَّهِ تَصِيرُ الْأُمُورُ (٥٣)).
His saying (صِرَاطِ اللَّهِ): it is a badal (substitute) of (صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ) — a definite substituted for an indefinite. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا لِتُنْذِرَ أُمَّ الْقُرَى وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا وَتُنْذِرَ يَوْمَ الْجَمْعِ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهِ فَرِيقٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ وَفَرِيقٌ فِي السَّعِيرِ (٧)).
His saying (فَرِيقٌ): it is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "some of them are a party in the Garden and some of them are a party in the Blaze". The implied wording may also be "among them is a party".

ukberi-tibyan:8-8.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَجَعَلَهُمْ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً وَلَكِنْ يُدْخِلُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ فِي رَحْمَتِهِ وَالظَّالِمُونَ مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا نَصِيرٍ (٨)).
His saying (وَالظَّالِمُونَ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and what follows it is the khabar (predicate). The accusative was not good, because in the clause after it there is no verb that would explain the governor of the accusative.
